current.note: R5.0a: gate is now class-breakdown aware and can run with either OCR engine (--ocr-engine legacy|lattice). Aggregate thresholds unchanged (D77 - this fazda yalnizca yukari hareket edebilir); classRecallThresholds only carries Hyphenation, at its measured value, per D76 (OCR classes stay unthresholded until R5.0d grows the ground truth past 12 records).

legacy.note: R4.0c: benchmark's OCR mutation stage measured with the legacy engine. CorrectlyFixed=148, WronglyFixed=0, Deferred=12 (precision 100%, recall 92.5%), matching this gate's thresholds unchanged. All 12 OCR-class ground-truth records (Fragmentation 5, GlyphConfusion 4, GarbageInsertion 2, SpuriousSpace 1) were Deferred, not WronglyFixed - the legacy engine's 120 mutations do not intersect any of the 160 ground-truth records (D64). Thresholds are not adjusted by this measurement (D63).

lattice.note: R5.0a: first benchmark run of the lattice engine via --ocr-engine lattice (previously impossible - plan section 6.1 point 2). Gate PASSES: precision 99.33% (>= 98%), recall 93.12% (>= 92.5%), ProtectedChanged=0, ProtectedViolated=0 (closes D48 for the lattice engine too). Lattice plans only 19 OCR mutations (vs legacy's 120) yet correctly fixes one more known error overall (149 vs 148): it fixes odun-kesmek-space-0001 ('koli ukta' -> 'koltukta', SpuriousSpace) that legacy left Deferred, and wrongly fixes odun-kesmek-garbage-0001 (':,ohbet' -> expected 'sohbet', observed ':,sohbet' - one character corrected, the leading garbage glyphs were not). Hyphenation is untouched by engine choice (its correction stage runs before and independently of ocrCorrectionPlanner), so its 100% recall is identical across both engines - this is why a class-recall floor can be set for it now without D63's overfitting risk. Not a like-for-like comparison with phase 4's book-health measurement (D65/D66) - this run only scores the 160 ground-truth records, not the whole book.
